summary:
Third and last technical review of phase D: submission sub-mv36aj2e-01cd090a (115 artifacts), iteration 3 of 3, which responds to rev-mv35hyoj-01e0a18c.

What I read:
- the d1, d2 and d3 diffs (git diff a9d0507 HEAD: 10 files, +596/-36, exactly the files the three handoffs declare);
- the reset handoffs ho-mv35op30-016a6560 (d1), ho-mv35z5ux-01b0d55a (d2) and ho-mv35zyof-011e9473 (d3), and handoff-3.json;
- the iteration-3 section of submission.md;

- npm run test:browser: 8/8 (ev:ev-mv36h45j-01fcf22e).
- Plan commands, verbatim:
  - d1: 154/154 (ev:ev-mv36h86l-019f5e11);
  - d2: 112/112, with ECCODE_EVAL 200/200 (ev:ev-mv36hv4x-01404237);
  - d3: 118/118 (ev:ev-mv36i2sl-01deb1fc);

- Artifact coverage: 113 declared, 112 changed, 0 undeclared, 0 outside ownership (ev:ev-mv36ovxm-01536507).
- My earlier probes, re-run by path: P5 (ev:ev-mv36n7ym-016a98f1), and P3 and P4 (ev:ev-mv36npp3-01cc274c).
- New probes P7-P11, 8/8 (ev:ev-mv36n2by-01c422d2):
  - P7: alignment;
  - P8: deadline times;
  - P9: the TR-D-14 route;
  - P10: the real gate after close(), after the adapter's timeout, and when closed before spawn;
  - P11: a real server on SIGHUP, and with repeated signals inside the grace period.
- 20 mutants of my own on the new code:
  - 18 are killed (ev:ev-mv36sh0c-019c0ced, ev:ev-mv36r8lf-01323bb3);
  - 2 survive (ev:ev-mv36q12a-0122343d). That run fails by design, because my driver fails on any survivor, and it is cited only in TR-D-18.

Resolved in this iteration:
- TR-D-11 (major, = SEC-D-12): all six conditions hold.
- TR-D-12 (= SEC-D-11).
- TR-D-14.
- TR-D-15 (= SEC-D-16), with FU-32 accepted.

Each is verified on HEAD by my own runs.

- TR-D-16 (info): the live runner's SIGHUP. Its disposition is FU-28 (b), owner ai-engineer with FU-26.

findings.title: A user_text deadline is grounded on its time only: the date part of the resolution condition is not met (FU-30, dec-mv36cgyj-01f0741d); Arabic am/pm is FU-31
findings.detail:
The time part is resolved. deadlineTimeInQuote (src/services/extraction.js L396) requires the value's HH:MM to be in the quote, as a clock token or an hour with am/pm, aligned like a number and inside an occurrence of the quote.

Verified:
- My P5c re-run by path (ev:ev-mv36n7ym-016a98f1) shows 06:00 'for the weekend', 23:59 'by 11:30' and 2026-10-21T06:00 'for the weekend' unknown, and 'by 11:30' known.
- P8 (ev:ev-mv36n2by-01c422d2) shows Arabic 'قبل الساعة ١١:٣٠', '3pm', '12 pm', '12 am', '1:30' and '11:30pm'->23:30 known. It shows unknown, and asked: '11:30' quoted 'by 11:30pm', '11.30', '211:30', '5 amps' and 'noon'.
- Mutants M12, M13 and M14 are killed (ev:ev-mv36sh0c-019c0ced).
- The named test is extract.test.js L283.

Not met: 'and its date part too when present'. P8 shows 2026-10-25T11:30 quoted 'on Friday by 11:30' known, and 2026-12-01T11:30 quoted 'on 21 Oct by 11:30' known, although the written date contradicts the value. The submission says so itself. The orchestrator recorded dec-mv36cgyj-01f0741d: an accepted residual for version one, owner backend-engineer, riding FU-23's rework-4 if the user authorizes it.

Why this stays minor and does not block:
- the buyer confirms every deadline, with the quote shown next to the value;
- the plan is approved before any payment;
- FU-31's unread Arabic markers fail in the safe direction (unknown, asked).
findings.recommendation:
Disposition: dec-mv36cgyj-01f0741d. FU-30 and FU-31 have owner backend-engineer, through the user-authorised rework of src/services/extraction.js. delivery-lead lists both in the verification report (carry item 9).

Resolved when FU-30's criterion lands: an absolute date written in the quote (ISO, '21 Oct', '21/10', and the Arabic forms) must equal the value's date, or the deadline is unknown and asked. The named test is 'SEC-7: a user_text deadline whose written date differs from its value is unknown (FU-30)'.

A cheap partial check FU-30 may add even without a calendar: a full date-time whose quote carries no date token at all, and whose day is not the request day, is unknown.

findings.title: Two mutants of the d2 adapter survive: M19 (the cap in terminate() is pre-empted by the close handler) and M21 (the 'never started is not charged' branch of fail() is untested)
findings.detail:
From my mutation run (ev:ev-mv36q12a-0122343d, which fails by design because my driver fails on any survivor).

- M19: removing the cap from terminate()'s rejection (src/ai/cli.js L198) leaves cli.test.js 38/38 green. When the child exits, Node emits 'close' right after 'exit' once stdio is closed, so the close handler of a terminated run (L246), which also carries unknownAtCap(), settles first. finish() is idempotent, so terminate()'s own rejection never wins in these runs. M19b (L246 only) and M19c (both sites) are killed (ev:ev-mv36r8lf-01323bb3), so the close() charge is pinned by tests. M19 is an equivalent mutant in practice, and L198 is a redundant backstop.
- M21: changing fail() to `usageHint ?? unknownAtCap()` (L206), which charges calls that never started a process, also leaves 38/38 green. The d2 test 'TR-D-15: a call that never started a process ... is not charged' (cli.test.js L467) covers two cases, and neither goes through fail():
  - a provider closed before call(), which is refused at the provider level;
  - a missing binary, which arrives as the child 'error' event.
  The fail() branches without a child are untested: close() while the temp cwd is being made, a signal aborted before the spawn, and a synchronous spawn throw. If that code were wrong, the error would over-charge, which is the conservative direction.

Neither affects the ledger behaviour I verified through the route (P10a, P10b, P10c) and on a real server (P11, P4).
findings.recommendation: Owner: ai-engineer, with the FU-26 adapter change (no later task owns src/ai/cli.js); not required for this phase. Add a test that reaches fail() without a child and asserts err.usage is undefined, for example close() raced against the mkdtemp, or a signal aborted between the call and the spawn. Either drop terminate()'s duplicate usage or comment that the close handler normally settles first. delivery-lead may note it under carry item 8.

resolvedFindings.resolution:
Resolved; this is also security's SEC-D-12. All six conditions hold.
(1) normaliseExtraction accepts provenance image only when hasImage is true and the field is in the frozen, exported IMAGE_PROVENANCE_FIELDS = productType, material, capacityMl, diameterMm (src/services/extraction.js L367, L436), as dec-mv35aank-0169ec16 decides. Any other image claim is downgraded to unknown with its template question, and the rest of the answer stands.
(2) The named route test, extract-image.test.js L175, uploads a real PNG and checks both the response and the stored fields_json. Budget 99999, maxPickups 5, cupQuantity and lidQuantity 99999 and deadline 06:00 are all unknown, with their questions. The unit-level twin is extract.test.js L336.
(3) RS-02 (extract-image.test.js L77) is green, and the EXT-1 fake eval is 200/200 in my npm test and d2 runs.
(4) My mutants are killed (ev:ev-mv36sh0c-019c0ced): M9 removes the allow-list (2 red), and M9b replaces it with a budget-only deny-list (2 red).
(5) npm test, the d3 command and the browser suite pass.
(6) My P5, re-run by path (ev:ev-mv36n7ym-016a98f1): with a photo, P5a and P5b show budgetCents, maxPickups, cupQuantity and the deadline unknown. Without a photo, everything is unknown. capacityMl 1999 'image' stays known, which is the accepted SEC-D-14 residual.

Resolved. d3 removed its local substring check. quoteGrounded (extraction.js L357) now runs d1's validateExtraction with the text for every user_text field, numeric or not (L432), so one guard serves every field kind.

The named test extract.test.js L312 stores these unknown, with their questions: material 'plastic' quoted 'plastic cups', productType 'lids' quoted 'lids only', and a deadline quoted 'by noon, 11:00'. Empty and null quotes are unknown too. The grounded forms stay known. My P9 shows the same through the route (ev:ev-mv36n2by-01c422d2).

My M2 no longer exists as a line, so I ran its equivalents (ev:ev-mv36sh0c-019c0ced):

- M11, the quote check kept for numbers (and deadlines) only: 2 red, the TR-D-14 tests.

Resolved; this is also security's SEC-D-16. d2 was reset. A call ended by close() rejects PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE with the per-call cap as its usage, in the full usage shape (cli.js L246, L287). gate.run then settles at the cap.

The real gate through the route:
- my P10a (ev:ev-mv36n2by-01c422d2) and my P3c re-run (ev:ev-mv36npp3-01cc274c) show the row reserved 50000 while the stub runs, and settled 50000/50000 after close(); the response is 200, degraded, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE;
- on a real server, P4 SIGTERM and P11 SIGHUP leave the row settled at the cap;
- P4 SIGKILL leaves the row reserved, which is the FU-28 residual the startup sweep settles.

The suite's regression guard is cli.test.js L437 (the real gate and SQLite). The HTTP-level row test that carry item 8 says nobody wrote is replaced, as evidence for this phase, by my P3c, P10a and P11 runs. Mutants M22, M19b and M19c are killed. M19 and M21 survive (TR-D-18, info).

FU-32: I accept the extension, as dec-mv36cgqs-01f68eb5 records. Once a child has started, the real spend is unknown and bounded by the cap, so charging the cap on the adapter's own timeout, an abort or a flood keeps the ledger conservative, and it matches the service watchdog. P10b shows the adapter's own timeout settled at the cap. P10c shows a call on a closed provider spawns nothing and settles at 0. The cost is that a buyer who abandons a call is charged the cap against their own share. That is acceptable, and delivery-lead states it in the verification report.

Resolved as mapped.
- SEC-D-13 and SEC-D-14 are in carry item 6, and lexical grounding is dec-mv36ch5t-01a1d509.
- SEC-D-17 is fixed by the d2 reset: the cli.test.js sandbox PATH is the stub directory alone, providers get the stub as an absolute command, and the exit hook removes the temp cwd. 'SEC-D-17: the sandbox PATH is the stub directory alone ...' (cli.test.js L476) passes in my d2 run.
